text:
maya: heads-up — customer reported requests hitting public pools even when they have a private endpoint + workspace binding. seeing ~2% leakage during heavy traffic :thinking_face:
oliver: hmm. logs show X-Workspace-ID header present, but routing decided pool match by token tenant instead of header.
jamie: is this the same tenant affinity change we shipped last month? could be precedence rules.
maya: looks related. quick dump from gateway for one trace:
```
match: path=/v1/generate, token_tenant=ws-42, header_workspace=ws-42, vpc_endpoint=10.2.1.5, pool_affinity=dedicated-ws-42
decision: route -> public-pool-2 (reason: pool_affinity unavailable, fallback=public)
```

kevin: why did it ignore vpc_endpoint and header? our policy should prefer: workspace VPC -> dedicated pool -> workspace header -> token tenant -> poolless fallback.
oliver: current implementation computes affinity from token first and treats header as hint only when token doesn't map. that'll bite multi-tenant private endpoints.
sophie: we added that to avoid header spoofing attacks. header was untrusted unless signed by gateway. maybe the validation failed intermittently.
jamie: can we check the header validation failures in the same trace?
maya: yep. validation logs show "signature-missing" for ~3 requests in the burst window. but the header was set by the customer's LB. suspiciously only during autoscale events.
kevin: autoscale-related header rewrite? cloud egress LB sometimes strips custom headers for short-lived workers. we should treat vpc source IP as higher confidence than header signature.
oliver: agreed. proposal: compute routing precedence as: 1) private endpoint IP range (VPC) + workspace-binding, 2) signed workspace header, 3) token tenant mapping, 4) dedicated pool affinity, 5) public fallback. this makes VPC strongest signal.
sophie: we can keep header-signing to prevent spoofing but accept VPC source as implicit trust if it matches customer's registered CIDR. need a config flag for customers who use shared NAT though.
jamie: also need to adjust telemetry to emit which signal triggered the decision (enum: VPC, HEADER_SIGNED, TOKEN, POOL_AFFINITY, FALLBACK). console should show per-request routing reason.
maya: +1. product wants a rollout UX: start with "log-only" mode for a week to measure how many requests would flip. also add a quota safeguard: do not route to private pool if it would exceed reserved capacity -> instead mark as "would_route_private_over_quota" in logs.
kevin: implementation plan: gateway change + small agent to fetch registered CIDRs from control plane cache, header verifier tweak, telemetry enum, and console flag. timeline: 2 sprints for server + tests.
oliver: can we make this opt-in per-tenant? default to current behavior to avoid surprising customers. maybe enable for tenants with "private_endpoint: true" and an allowlist flag.
sophie: agree opt-in. we'll also document risks: NAT/shared IP, LB header stripping, and the spoofing mitigations.
maya: action items:
- oliver: PR to reorder precedence and add enum telemetry (due in 3 days)
- kevin: CIDR cache + control plane endpoint (RFC by Friday)
- jamie: console "routing reason" column + rollout toggle (mockups Monday)
- sophie: docs + security note (doc draft next Wed)

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: run gateway integration tests, simulate header strip and VPC CIDR flows, smoke test with staging tenant.
oliver: I'll open a draft PR and include simulated traces. tagging @team-security for header-signing review.
maya: thanks. keeping this thread as source of truth. ping if anyone sees unexpected routing flips after opt-in rollout. :thumbsup:
